The presence of significant central necrosis (NCR Volume (mL) of 27.773) and a thick enhancing margin (>3mm) are hallmark features of glioblastoma, which is the most common IDH-wildtype tumor. The most definitive feature is the presence of a large necrotic core (NCR Volume (mL): 27.773). In the context of a diffusely infiltrating glioma in an adult, radiologically evident necrosis is a surrogate for microvascular proliferation and/or necrosis on histology, which are criteria for WHO grade 4. This is further supported by the presence of contrast enhancement (ET Volume (mL): 22.626) with a thick margin (>3mm), extensive peritumoral edema, and significant mass effect causing midline shift. There are no features to suggest a lower grade (2 or 3), as grade 2 tumors are typically non-enhancing and grade 3 tumors usually lack extensive central necrosis.
